title: Adjacent sortedness equals pairwise sortedness
statement: Let $\mathit{xs}$ be a finite list over a linearly ordered set. Then $\mathit{xs}$ is sorted in the adjacent-pairs sense if and only if it is sorted in the usual pairwise sense with respect to $\le$; that is, if and only if $x_i \le x_j$ for every pair of indices $i < j$.
hypotheses_covered: xs is a list over a linearly ordered type
replaced:
For any list $\mathit{xs}$, the predicate \texttt{IsSorted} holds of $\mathit{xs}$ if and only if
$\mathit{xs}$ is sorted in the usual pairwise sense with respect to $\le$.
